title: closure-rule-language
description: The formal first-order language in which closure rules are written - positive in the cell values, with a single forall-block over entities, with primitives inherited from the parameter base (L, C, E, lambda). It is the grammar generated from closure-rule by spelling out its atomic formulas, antecedent shape, and consequent.

atomicFormulas.description: the two kinds of atom that may appear in antecedents

cellAtom.description: v(q)(s1, s2) >=_k V for q in C and value V in L^bowtie; asserts a >=_k lower bound on the cell value, positive in the knowledge order

signatureAtom.description: a literal in the inherited signature: relations from E, the four-generator structure from C, and residuated-lattice relations from L

antecedentShape.description: a positive Boolean combination of atoms under at most a single universal block

positive.description: conjunction and disjunction of atoms with no negation, so the language is monotone in the cell values

quantifierBlock.description: optionally preceded by one block forall x_1 ... forall x_n of universal quantifiers over entity variables

consequentShape.description: a single cell-update assertion v'(p)(t1, t2) >=_k V with p in C, entity terms in the free variables, and value V in the knowledge order

quantifierComplexity.description: the antecedent quantifier structure determines Scott-continuity of the generated closure operator

quantifierFreeIsScottContinuous.description: a quantifier-free antecedent is Scott-continuous; each cell atom commits at a finite stage of any directed family

infiniteForallIsNonScottContinuous.description: a forall-block over an infinite domain commits only at the limit, the syntactic origin of non-Scott-continuous firing ordinals and the transfinite-bounded and aperiodic regimes
